records.plant_name: Switch Grand Rapids Data Center power station

verifications.note: State air permit 112-16A, version 4.0, issued September 29, 2026, to MI GRR, LLC at 6100 East Paris Avenue, Grand Rapids. Lists 2,740 kilowatt diesel emergency engines.
Switch's own page for its Pyramid campus in Grand Rapids.

records.researcher_notes: Switch runs the Pyramid campus data center at 6100 East Paris Avenue in Gaines Township, Grand Rapids, Kent County. The state air permit 112-16A, version 4.0, was issued on September 29, 2026 to MI GRR, LLC for that address. It lists 39 diesel emergency engines, numbered EUEG4 through EUEG42, of 2,740 kilowatts each. That is 106.86 MW. The permit repeats the same 39 engines under two groups of engines, so the earlier permit harvest total of 78 engines and 213.7 MW counted them twice. A separate 90 kilowatt fire pump is left out. The engines were installed from 2017 through April 2026. The permit says the building will be taken off the grid for a planned outage in October 2026. Not found: the owner of MI GRR, LLC by name in a source, and the coordinates, which the location step still has to place. Switch's own page names the Pyramid campus but does not name this company. Location: the permit gives 6100 East Paris Avenue. The Census geocoder puts that address on the road at 42.85254, -85.56538. In satellite imagery the Switch pyramid data center building and its engine yard sit about 400 meters east of that point on the same side of the road, so the point is placed on the pyramid building.

records.plant_name: Google Van Buren Township Data Center power station

verifications.note: State air permit to install PTI0000209, version 1.0, issued July 30, 2026, to Panattoni Development Company at 10385 Haggerty Road. Lists 24 emergency engines of 2,750 kilowatts.
CBS Detroit, March 17, 2026: Google is behind the Van Buren Township data center plan and the land is under agreement with Panattoni.
Planet Detroit, February 2026: Panattoni's preliminary site plan for Project Cannoli at Haggerty Road.

records.researcher_notes: The state air permit to install PTI0000209, version 1.0, was issued on July 30, 2026 to Panattoni Development Company at 10385 Haggerty Road, Van Buren Charter Township, Wayne County. It lists 24 emergency engines of 2,750 kilowatts each that burn diesel or renewable diesel. That is 66.0 MW. Two 170 horsepower fire pumps are left out. Panattoni's application response letter of June 5, 2026 says it cut the proposed engines from 155 to 24. A Planet Detroit story from February 2026 quoted Panattoni as saying 156 diesel generators. CBS Detroit reported in March 2026 that Google is behind the project and that the land is under agreement with Panattoni, so the plant is named for Google. The township approved the final site plan in October 2026 and reports say site work began in August. The permit alone fits pre-construction, so that is the status here. A reviewer may choose construction if site work is confirmed. Not found: the start year and the coordinates. Location: the permit gives 10385 Haggerty Road. The Census geocoder puts that address on the road at 42.22707, -83.44481. Satellite imagery shows open farmland east of the road with no buildings yet, so the point is placed in the field just east of the address and stays approximate because the parcel lines were not seen.

records.plant_name: Raeden Gibraltar Data Center power station

verifications.note: Planet Detroit, March 12, 2026: Raeden's proposed 100 MW Gibraltar data center would have 30 to 35 backup diesel generators. The same article gives the site address, an existing building at 27800 W. Jefferson Ave. on the former McLouth Steel property, with the Humbug Marsh directly across the road.

records.researcher_notes: Planet Detroit reported on March 12, 2026 that the developer Raeden plans a 100 megawatt data center on the former McLouth Steel site in Gibraltar, Wayne County. Its chief operating officer said it would have 30 to 35 backup diesel generators. The city passed a one year moratorium on data centers on March 9, 2026, and the developer may ask for a waiver. No air permit application, generator size or coordinates were found. The capacity is left blank. The engine count is the high end of the range. Location: the Planet Detroit report gives the address, an existing building at 27800 W. Jefferson Ave. on the former McLouth Steel property in Gibraltar, with the Humbug Marsh across the road. The Census address search places 27800 W. Jefferson Ave. at 42.10629, -83.19680. A satellite look shows the former McLouth mill buildings on the west side of West Jefferson Avenue at that point, with marsh and woods on the east side, which matches the report. The point stays approximate because the report also names an adjacent Superfund lot at 28000 W. Jefferson, and the line between the two lots was not found. The report says that lot could host natural gas generation; no plan for it was found.
